newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, DEC 2 - SUNDAY, DEC 8 1996.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, DEC 2 - SUNDAY, DEC 8 1996.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS

BRUSSELS - EU finance ministers meet (Monday); preparation for third stage of EMU including discussions on the legal status of the Euro, relationships between participating and non-participating countries and stability pact.

BRUSSELS - EU social affairs ministers meet (Monday); burden of proof in sex discrimination cases and implementing the principle of equal treatment between men and women in employment and professional promotions and working conditions (Kalanke European Court of Justice judgment).

BRUSSELS - EU energy ministers meet (Tuesday); orientation debate on regulations for a single market in natural gas; open debate on a strategy on renewable energy and adoption of a multi-annual programme to promote international cooperation in the energy sector.

BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday); statement on competition aspects of the privatisation of Thomson SA electronics group; discussion on common organisation of tobacco market.
BRUSSELS - EU research ministers meet (Thursday).
BRUSSELS - European Commission President Santer meets Irish Prime Minister John Bruton; meets Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi (Thursday).
BRUSSELS - European People's Party holds pre-Dublin European Council summit (Thursday).
BRUSSELS - General Affairs Council; discussions focus on Dublin European Council, Mediterranean policy, relations with central and Eastern Europe and trans-Atlantic relations (Friday).
DUBLIN - EU social affairs ministers hold informal meeting (Friday).
MONDAY, DECEMBER 2
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - ECOFIN Council.
Agenda includes:
- EIB loans to third countries:
- New lending mandates for central and East European countries, Mediterranean, Asia, Latin America and South Africa;
- Interim lending mandate for Asia and Latin America.
- SEM 2000 (sound and efficient management) final report of personal representatives group.
- Preparation for December 13-14 Dublin European summit:
- Preparation for third stage of EMU - legal status of the Euro, relationships between participating and non-participating countries and stability pact;
- Employment.
- Specific arrangements for travellers' allowances granted to Nordic countries and standard VAT rate.
- Preparation of the Dutch presidency's working programme.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Social Affairs Council (1000/0900 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Follow-up to the Essen European Council: draft single report to the European Council of Dublin.
- Proposal for Council decision on the creation of a political committee for employment and the labour market.

- Proposal for a directive modifying directive 76/207/EEC on the implementation of the principle of equal treatment between men and women in employment and professional promotions and working conditions (Kalanke European Court of Justice judgment).
- Draft resolution on equal rights for the disabled.
- Draft resolution on the role of systems for social protection and the fight against unemployment.

- Proposal for Council regulation on the modification of regulation 1408/71 on the application of the social security regime for salaried workers and self-employed people and their families who move within the EU, and to regulation 574/72 fixing modalities for the application of regulation 1408/71;
- Proposal for Council directive on health protection and worker's safety against risks related to exposure to chemical agents at work.
- Council conclusions on lifelong learning.
- Follow-up to the communication on "Worker information and consultation".
- Commission presents communication on "Development of the social dialogue at a Community level".
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (1500/1400 GMT) Foreign Affairs;
Agriculture;
Budget;
Economic;
Energy;
External Economic Relations;
Civil Liberties;
Institutional Affairs.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) holds conference on "EMU and the IGC" (and Tuesday).
Agenda includes:
- (1400/1300 GMT) Employment and EMU - DG II Director Ludwig Schubert gives address.
- (1630/1530 GMT) Importance of information on EMU - MEP Luciana Castellina gives address.
- (1730/1630 GMT) Information on medium-term priorities and action of the ETUC.
Venue: International Trade Union House, 155 Boulevard Emile Jacqmain. Contact: ETUC (322) 224 0403.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Edinburgh's Telford College hosts "The EU 1996 Helios II" competitions awards ceremony (1500/1400 GMT). Participants include: DG V Director General Allan Larsson. Venue: Concert Noble. Contact: Edinburgh's Telford College (44) 131 332 2491.

BRUSSELS - UNICE, in collaboration with the European Commission, holds conference on "Company consumer and consumer dialogue in Europe" (0915/0815 GMT). Agenda includes: review of past experience and recommendations for the future; institutionalised forms of dialogue; public and private ombudsman systems: different approaches; direct dialogue between companies and consumers: company initiatives. Speakers include: European Commissioner Emma Bonino, UNICE Chairman Francois Perigot and Secretary General Zygmunt Tyskiewicz; DG XXIV Director General Spyros Pappas. Venue: Borschette Centre. Contact: Jerome Chauvin, UNICE (322) 231 1445.
LONDON - Financial Times holds conference on "World telecoms - New alliances for a new era" (and Tuesday). Venue: Inter Continental Hotel. Contact: Financial Times (44) 171 896 2626.

LISBON - Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) holds annual summit. Main discussions will focus on outlining the principles and parameters of European security cooperation in the 21st century (and Tuesday).
(All venues Luxembourg, Plateau de Kirchberg)
TUESDAY, DECEMBER 3
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Energy Council (1000/0900 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Orientation debate and Council conclusions on common regulations for a single market in natural gas.
- (1200/1100 GMT) Commission presentation followed by an open debate on a strategy on renewable energy.
- Modified proposal for Council regulation on the adoption of a multi-annual programme to promote international cooperation in the energy sector - Synergy programme.
- Council conclusions on the report on the supply, refining and oil markets in the EU.
- Council conclusions on climate change - energy dimension.

- Commission communication and proposal for Council and Commission decision on the conclusion by the EU of the Energy Charter and of the Energy Charter protocol on energy efficiency and environmental aspects.
- Commission oral report on Euro-Mediterranean partnership in energy.
- Second Commission report on the revision of Community legislation in energy and Commission communication extending several Community legal texts in the energy sector.
- Proposal for decision on the modification of decision 1254/96/EC establishing a set of guidelines on trans-European networks in the energy sector.
- Commission presentation on the ALTERNER II decision.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Inter-governmental conference (IGC) representatives meet.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Fischler addresses the BSE inquiry committee.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission and U.S. agriculture officials meet; discussions focus on farm trade disputes ranging from EU grain import tariffs and wheat subsidies to a planned veterinary agreement. Participants include: U.S. trade adviser to U.S. Agriculture Secretary Paul Drazek and European Commissioner Fischler's Chief of Cabinet Corrado Pirzio-Biroli.
FRANKFURT (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner de Silguy visits the European Monetary Institute.
LISBON (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Brittan attends high-level EU-Canada meeting.

BRUSSELS - MEPs Mary Banotti and Barbara Schmidbauer hold joint news conference on "European day for the disabled - Rights of disabled" (1030/0930 GMT). Venue: EP building. Contact: Diana Sutton (322) 284 7529.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (0900/0800 GMT) Foreign Affairs;
Agriculture;
Budget;
Economic;
Energy;
External Economic Relations;
Civil Liberties;
Institutional Affairs;
- (1500/1400 GMT) Budget;
Civil Liberties.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Insitute for Asian Studies hosts briefing by MEP Glenys Kinnock on the current situation in Burma (1200/1100 GMT). Venue: European Insitute for Asian Studies, 35 rue des Deux Eglises. Contact: European Institute for Asian Studies (322) 230 8122.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) holds conference on "EMU and the IGC" (second of two days).
Agenda includes:
- (0930/0830 GMT) The ETUC and the IGC - trade union demands;
- (1030/0930 GMT) "Progress report" on the IGC;
- (1130/1030 GMT) The IGC and the social dimension;
- (1430/1330 GMT) Round table on "Is the IGC meeting the demands and expectations of workers and citizens?"

- Irish Labour Minister Fitzgerald; Dutch Labour Minister Melkert; European Commissioner Oreja; MEPS Elisabeth Guigou and Brok and ETUC Secretary General Emilio Gabaglio attend. Venue: International Trade Union House, 155 Boulevard Emile Jacqmain. Contact: ETUC (322) 224 0403.

BRUSSELS - Association of European Producers of Steel for Packaging (APEAL) holds press briefing on "Overturning the Danish can ban" (1030/0930 GMT). Venue: Bureau de Liaison Brussels-Europe, 63 avenue d'Auderghem. Contact: Georges Ellis, Hill and Knowlton (322) 640 0495.

BRUSSELS - Centre of European Policy Studies (CEPS) conference "Integrating rural development policies in the EU: a panacea for European agriculture?" (0845/0745 GMT). Speakers include: MEP Lord Plumb, COPA Secretary General Peter Polley. Venue: CEPS. Contact: Isabelle Tenaerts (322) 229 3956.
WEDNESDAY, DECEMBER 4
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0800 GMT).
Provisional agenda incudes:
- Statement on competition aspects of the privatisation of the Thomson SA electronics group.
- European Commissioner Fischler communication on common organisation of tobacco market.
- European Commissioner Flynn on current and envisaged Community role in the fight against tobacco consumption.
- European Commissioner Bjerregaard communications on introduction into the EU of furs and products from certain wild animal species, on ecolabels and on environmental responsibility.
- European Commissioners Cresson, Bangemann and Kinnock communication on EU and space.
- European Commission President Santer presents Dutch EU Presidency work programme.
LONDON (NEW ITEM) - European Commission hosts information and sources meeting "The INFO 2000 programme" (0845/0845 GMT). Venue: Hilton Olympia, Tower room.

BRUSSELS - European Radical Alliance (ERA) holds hearing on employment "Labour: for a new approach" (0930/0830 GMT). Agenda includes: evolution of the notion "Labour"; proposals for a new social contract. Venue: EP, MAE 3 room. Contact: Fatma Thorinius-Fall (322) 284 2259.
BASEL, Switzerland - Assembly of European Regions (AER) holds general assembly (and Thursday). Contact: AER (33) 88 32 84 97.

LONDON - Britain hosts international conference on peace consolidation in Bosnia in 1997. Meeting will be attended by some 50 countries and international agencies as well as by newly-elected Bosnian leaders (To December 5).

LONDON - Financial Times (FT) holds conference on "Venture '96 Europe" (to Friday). Main topics discussed: overview of venture capital and buyout markets in Europe; update on eastern Europe; fund raising for European investments; technology - a hot investment sector; mezzanine and senior debt - a look at availability and terms; managing the European portfolio; deal flow channels; exit and IPO markets in Europe. Contact: FT conferences (44) 171 896 2626.
THURSDAY, DECEMBER 5
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Research Council (1000/0900 GMT).
Agenda includes:
- Draft Council conclusions on research on TSE.
- Second adaptation of the fourth research framework programme.
- Draft Council conclusions on SMEs and framework research programme.
- Commission communication and draft Council conclusions on the role of Joint Research Centre.
- Exchange of views on the fifth framework programme.
- Draft Council conclusions on the role of research in the fight against drugs.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer meets Irish Prime Minister John Bruton; meets Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts conference on "The role, position and liability of the statutory auditor in the EU" (and Friday). Contact: Marie-Christine Batt, DGXV (322) 295 1343.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European People's Party (EPP) holds pre-Dublin European Council summit (1915/1815 GMT). EPP President Wilfried Martens holds closing news conference at 2200/2100 GMT. Participants include: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Spanish Prime Minister Jose Aznar, Irish Prime Minister John Bruton, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Junker and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and European Commissioner President Santer. Venue: EP building, ESL room 6B54.
BRUSSELS - European Environmental Bureau (EEB) hold seminar on "Ecolabel sells?". Venue: Borschette centre. Contact: EEB (322) 539 0037.
DRESDEN, Germany - European Environmental Research Organisation holds conference on "Introduction of genetically modified organisms into the environment: biosafety aspects" (To December 12).
FRIDAY, DECEMBER 6
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - General Affairs Council.
Provisional agenda includes:
- In the morning - preparation for Dublin European Council.
- Mediterranean policy;
- Report on the follow-up to the Barcelona conference;
- Negotiations for an agreement with the PLO.
- Relations with central and eastern European countries:
- Adaptation of the Europe agreements following enlargement and the conclusion of the Uruguay Round (agriculture).
- Trans-Atlantic relations:
- Preparation for EU/U.S. summit and future of EU/Canada relations.
- Relations with Switzerland.
- Proposal for a Council decision on the mid-term review of Council decision 91/482/EEC of July 25, 1991 on the association of the overseas countries and territories with the EU:
- trade arrangements.
- Monitoring Centre for racism and xenophobia.
- Situation in former Yugoslavia.
- Situation in the Middle East.
- Current situation of the inter-governmental conference (IGC).
- Future relations with Cuba.
- In the margins of the Council - European Economic Area Ministerial Council
- In the afternoon - EU foreign ministers hold conclave to prepare for Dublin European Council.
- Conference of representatives of the governments of the member states discuss seat of the Community Plant Variety Office.
DUBLIN (NEW ITEM) - EU social affairs ministers hold informal meeting.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Radical Antiprohibitionist Coordination (CORA) holds VIII congress (1500/1400 GMT). Speakers include: European Commissioner Bonino, MEPs Daniel Cohn-Bendit and Bernard Kouchner and former Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Martino. Venue: EP Maerlant, room MAE3. Contact: CORA (39) 2 2 304121.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Environmental Bureau (EEB) holds news conference on "The fight against desertification" (1100/1000 GMT). Participants include: Senegal Environment Minister Abdoulaye Bathily. Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: EEB (322) 539 0037.

PARIS - Group of the Party of European Socialists holds debate on "Europe on the eve of the millennium" (1100/1000 GMT). Speakers include: MEPs Enrique Baron Crespo and Simone Veil; former European Commission President Jacques Delors. Venue: EP, 288 boulevard Saint-Germain. Contact: Ambroise Perrin (322) 284 3062.
SATURDAY, DECEMBER 7
No events scheduled.
SUNDAY, DECEMBER 8
No events scheduled.
